readings.reading: The few cells in one corner are completed into a pattern with four-fold symmetry about the grid centre; where a ring's corner cell has a neighbouring mark two cells along the ring, that mark's colour is repeated on every other cell along the ring's edges between the mirrored corners.
readings.why: output is symmetric about both centre lines; every ring with a side mark has a full alternating dotted edge of that mark colour

readings.reading: The motif in one corner is completed to 4-fold symmetry about the grid centre; where a mirrored pair of cells on one row or column has a different-coloured cell two steps inward, that colour is repeated every second cell between the pair (dotted edge lines).
readings.why: output = D4 overlay of input plus dotted lines; mirrored pairs without a step-2 neighbour (e.g. the 8s in pair 2) get no dots

readings.reading: The corner pattern is completed with 4-fold mirror symmetry about the grid's centre row and column; a colour that sits one gap away from a corner element along a row/column is continued as a dotted line (every other cell) until the mirrored copy of that element.
readings.why: output is symmetric about both centre axes, and each seeded row/column carries an alternating dotted line between the two mirrored corner elements

readings.reading: The few coloured cells in one corner are completed to full 4-fold (D4) symmetry about the grid centre; then the colour sitting two steps from a corner cell along its row/column is drawn as a dotted line (every second cell) between that corner and its mirror images, forming a dotted square frame.
readings.why: the output is D4-symmetric and each dotted side runs between two mirror copies of the same corner cell with period 2

readings.reading: The corner pattern is completed to four-fold symmetry about the grid centre, and each outer ring side is drawn as a dotted line (every second cell) in the colour of the mark next to the corner, running from corner to corner.
readings.why: output is symmetric about both central axes and each outer side is a period-2 run between its two corners

readings.reading: A partially drawn symmetric pattern is completed so that the output is symmetric about both its horizontal and vertical centre lines.
readings.why: the output is mirror-symmetric left-right and top-bottom; every input fg cell is kept

readings.reading: The partial pattern is completed so the grid is symmetric under flips and transpose (D4); fg cells are overlaid with their mirror images.
readings.why: output equals the overlay of the input with its horizontal, vertical and diagonal mirror images (pair 1 needs the diagonal)

readings.reading: The partial pattern is completed so the output is symmetric (left-right, up-down and diagonal) about the grid centre.
readings.why: the output is the input plus its reflections about the grid's centre axes (and diagonal); no input fg cell changes

readings.reading: A partly drawn symmetric pattern is completed so that the output is symmetric about the grid's centre axes (both mirrors and the diagonal).
readings.why: output equals the union of the input and its D4 images about the grid centre

readings.reading: Missing parts of a symmetric pattern are filled so the output is symmetric about the grid's central axes.
readings.why: output is symmetric (horizontal, vertical and diagonal) about the grid centre and contains every input fg cell

readings.reading: The big rectangle is projected outward to the grid border in all four directions as full-width bands, but any single row or column of a band that contains a scattered marker is left out entirely; markers stay.
readings.why: every lane from the rectangle to the border is either fully rectangle-coloured (no marker in it) or untouched (contains a marker)

readings.reading: The big colour-2 rectangle extends to the grid border in all four directions along each of its rows and columns, except lanes on a side that contain a marker cell; those lanes stay empty (markers kept).
readings.why: every background cell in a block row/column lane outside the block becomes 2 unless a marker lies in that lane on that side

readings.reading: The big colour-2 rectangle shoots full-width/height bands of 2 in all four directions through each of its rows and columns, except a row/column-side that contains a marker, which stays empty.
readings.why: every cell in a rectangle row/column outside the rectangle on a side with no marker becomes 2; sides with a marker are untouched

readings.reading: Every row and column of the solid block is extended in its direction (left, right, up, down) to the grid border in the block colour, except a row/column segment that contains a marker on that side, which is left empty (the marker stays).
readings.why: a ray from the block side is drawn to the border iff no marker lies on it

readings.reading: The big rectangle extends each of its rows and columns outward to the grid border in all four directions, except rows/columns that contain a marker on that side, which are not extended at all.
readings.why: every unblocked rectangle row/column is filled to the border; blocked ones stay empty

readings.reading: A background cell becomes 4 when four 2-cell segments of colour 1 point at it from left, right, above and below, each with a one-cell gap.
readings.why: exactly the cells with colour-1 cells at distances 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions become 4

readings.reading: Where four 2-cell dominoes point at one background cell from left, right, above and below (each ending two cells away), that centre cell becomes 4.
readings.why: the only changed cells are background cells with fg at distance 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions; each becomes 4

readings.reading: A background cell becomes 4 when four 2-cell segments of 1 point at it from left, right, up and down, each separated from it by one gap cell.
readings.why: exactly the cells with 1s at distances 2 and 3 in all four orthogonal directions turn 4

readings.reading: Wherever four 2-cell bars (left, right, above, below) point at one background cell from distance 2, that centre cell is coloured 4.
readings.why: exactly the cells with fg at offsets +-2 and +-3 along both row and column become 4

readings.reading: A background cell that is the centre of a plus formed by four dominoes (two cells at distance 2-3 in each of the four directions) becomes 4.
readings.why: exactly the plus-centre cells become colour 4; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Inside a 7 rectangle a 2 cell has a tail of 6s; a ray from the 2 continues away from the tail through the 7 interior, and the first frame cell it reaches is recoloured 7.
readings.why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 opposite its 6 tail, and it becomes 7

readings.reading: A line of 6s ends in a 2; a ray shot from the 2 away from the 6s crosses the 7 field and the first frame cell it hits turns 7.
readings.why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 (direction 2 minus adjacent 6), and it becomes 7 (7 is the background)

readings.reading: The 6-line ending in a 2 points a direction; continuing from the 2 in that direction through the 7 interior, the first border-band cell hit is turned to 7.
readings.why: only one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 (direction 6->2), which becomes 7

readings.reading: Inside the 7 rectangle a line of 6s ends in a 2 head; a ray continues from the head in that direction through the 7s, and the first cell it reaches outside the rectangle (in the coloured frame) becomes 7. Nothing else changes.
readings.why: exactly one cell changes: the first non-7 cell on the ray from the 2 away from the 6s

readings.reading: The 6-line with a 2 at its head points a ray from the 2 through the 7 area; the first frame cell (non-7) the ray hits becomes 7.
readings.why: only the first non-7 cell along the pointer's direction changes, to 7

readings.reading: Each 2 that lies inside a 3 rectangle gets a 3x3 ring of 1 drawn around it (overwriting whatever is there, even outside the rectangle); 2s lying in the 0 background get nothing.
readings.why: every 8-neighbour of a 2 having at least two orthogonal 3-neighbours becomes 1, except such 2s themselves; nothing else changes

readings.reading: Every 2 cell lying inside (or on the edge of) a green rectangle gets a 3x3 ring of 1 around it, the 2 kept in the centre; 2s outside rectangles are left alone.
readings.why: unit is the 3x3 block 111/121/111 centred on each anchor; overlapping copies keep the anchor 2s (adjacent anchors occur in pairs 1 and 2); rings may overwrite 0 and outside 2s

readings.reading: Each 2 lying inside a green (3) rectangle gets its 8 neighbours painted 1 (a 3x3 halo), overwriting whatever is there except other such 2s; 2s outside the rectangles get no halo.
readings.why: every 8-neighbour of a 2 that has 3 both vertically and horizontally adjacent becomes 1; the seeds themselves stay 2

readings.reading: Each 2 cell lying inside the bounding box of a 3 block gets a 3x3 ring of 1 around it (overwriting whatever is there, centre stays 2); 2s outside the blocks get nothing.
readings.why: every changed cell is an 8-neighbour of an in-block 2 and becomes 1; in-block 2s remain 2

readings.reading: Every 2 lying inside the bounding box of a 3-block gets a ring of 1s on all eight neighbours (overwriting 3, 0 or outside 2s); 2s outside the blocks are untouched.
readings.why: all 8-neighbours of in-block 2s (except in-block 2s) become 1; nothing else changes

readings.reading: The grid is a lattice of identical framed 2x2 tiles; when two tiles in the same tile-row or tile-column carry the same odd colour at the same sub-position, every tile between them gets that colour at that sub-position.
readings.why: for every sub-position, marks of one colour form unbroken runs between the two original marks along tile-rows/columns

readings.reading: The grid is a lattice of 4x4 boxes (period 5). An odd-coloured cell that appears at the same in-box position in two boxes of the same box-row or box-column is copied into that position of every box between them.
readings.why: changed cells are exactly the in-between positions of same-colour, same-position anomaly pairs along box rows/columns

readings.reading: The grid is a lattice of identical 2x2-interior boxes; when two boxes in the same box-row or box-column share an odd cell (same position in the box, same non-standard colour), every box between them gets that cell too.
readings.why: only interior cells at the shared position of boxes lying between a matching pair change, to the pair's colour

readings.reading: The grid is a lattice of identical small framed panels; when two panels in the same panel-row or panel-column carry the same unusual colour at the same inner position, every panel between them gets that colour at that position.
readings.why: for each offset, each panel-row and panel-column, the anomaly colour fills the span between its two occurrences

readings.reading: In a lattice of identical small tiles, when two tiles in the same tile-row or tile-column carry the same odd colour at the same position, every tile between them gets that colour at that position.
readings.why: for each position, odd colours form unbroken runs between matching tiles along tile-rows/columns

readings.reading: The right column and bottom row carry matching runs of colours; each colour c fills the block where its rows in the right column cross its columns in the bottom row.
readings.why: every cell whose row key equals its column key takes that colour; all others stay

readings.reading: The bottom row and the right column carry runs of colours; each colour fills the rectangle whose columns are its run in the bottom row and whose rows are its run in the right column.
readings.why: background cell (Y,X) takes colour c exactly when the bottom-row cell in column X and the right-column cell in row Y both have colour c; colour is that shared c (per cell), not a constant

readings.reading: The last column and last row each list colour runs; every cell whose row's last-column colour equals its column's last-row colour is filled with that colour, giving a diagonal of blocks.
readings.why: cell (y,x) gets colour c exactly when lastcol[y] = lastrow[x] = c; all other cells unchanged

readings.reading: The bottom row and right column are colour keys; each cell (y, x) whose right-column cell at row y and bottom-row cell at column x have the same colour c becomes c, giving a staircase of blocks along the anti-diagonal.
readings.why: every changed cell has matching key colours in its row (right edge) and column (bottom edge)

readings.reading: The bottom row and right column are colour keys; each interior cell whose column key equals its row key takes that colour, forming coloured blocks on the diagonal.
readings.why: a cell is coloured C exactly when bottom[X] = right[Y] = C

readings.reading: The input is copied twice side by side.
readings.why: output is a 1x2 arrangement of exact input copies

readings.reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
readings.why: output is a 1x2 tiling of the input in every pair

readings.reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
readings.why: output is 1x2 blocks, each an exact copy of the input

readings.reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
readings.why: output is a 1x2 tiling of the input with both blocks filled

readings.reading: The input is repeated twice side by side.
readings.why: output is a 1x2 row of input copies

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.
readings.why: every output block is the input, and the block count per side equals the input's distinct colour count

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k x k times, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.
readings.why: output size is 3k x 3k with every block equal to the input; k matches distinct colour count, not pixel or object count

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.
readings.why: every block of the output is the input; block count per side equals the number of colours

readings.reading: The 3x3 input is tiled k by k, where k is the number of distinct colours in the input.
readings.why: output size is 3k x 3k and every block equals the input; neither pixel_count nor object_count gives k on all pairs

readings.reading: The input is tiled N x N times, where N is the number of distinct colours in the input.
readings.why: every block of the N x N output is the input, N = number of distinct colours
